standard.title: Interpret and translate texts with cultural explanation
standard.description: interpret and translate a range of non-verbal, spoken and written texts, and explain how meaning is conveyed to reflect cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret and translate across cultural contexts, manage register conversion, and produce bilingual texts for public purposes (AC9LCH8C04). They have interpreted for visitors and created bilingual resources. They have not yet interpreted puns, sarcasm and malapropisms, created multimodal bilingual resources, or justified cultural communication decisions in diverse social scenarios.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret and translate a range of texts — including humour, sarcasm, puns and culturally-complex language — explaining how meaning is conveyed to reflect cultural context, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Interpreting humour, sarcasm and wordplay
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret puns, idioms, humour, sarcasm and malapropisms between target language and English, applying strategies to explain meaning including hidden or layered meanings.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least two examples of puns, sarcasm, or malapropisms, explaining the literal meaning, the intended meaning, and the strategy used to convey the correct meaning in translation.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret puns, idioms, humour and sarcasm; explain hidden meanings in malapropisms; apply strategies to make humorous intent translatable; discuss challenges of conveying tone-dependent meaning across cultural contexts; use dictionaries and digital tools to understand emerging new words and expressions.
wider: Research a specific form of target language humour — explain how it works linguistically and culturally, why it is difficult to translate, and what strategies are most effective
Compare how sarcasm or irony is signalled differently in the target language and English — identify what a translator must understand to convey the intended tone accurately
nodes.hinge_reason: Interpreting tone-dependent and culturally-layered meaning is the defining challenge of advanced translation and mediation. Students who cannot manage humour, sarcasm and wordplay cannot produce culturally appropriate interpretation for the full range of authentic texts they will encounter.

response_modes.reason: Humour and sarcasm interpretation requires students to analyse the literal-versus-intended meaning gap systematically, understand what cultural knowledge is required, and select a strategy. Explicit strategy instruction with varied examples builds the analytical translation capacity.

success_criteria: Interprets at least two examples of puns, sarcasm, or malapropisms
Explains the literal meaning, intended meaning, and translation strategy for each

nodes.label: Justifying cultural communication decisions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply non-verbal and spoken communication strategies across diverse social scenarios and justify their own communication decisions in terms of cultural context.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in at least one culturally diverse social scenario and explain at least two communication decisions made — describing the cultural logic behind each choice.
nodes.typical_width: Apply non-verbal and spoken communication strategies in a range of cultural contexts — dining, professional meetings, social occasions; justify own communication decisions; explain cultural protocols; demonstrate politeness, respect and formality appropriate to each context.
wider: Simulate a formal cultural scenario — business card exchange, formal dining, welcoming ceremony — and provide a post-simulation analysis explaining every cultural communication decision
Compare the cultural communication conventions for a specific scenario across two different target language community contexts — identify where conventions differ and what the differences reveal

response_modes.reason: Cultural communication justification requires practice across varied scenarios — professional, social, ceremonial. The same ability to explain communication decisions must transfer across different cultural contexts before students can justify their choices independently.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners often navigate diverse cultural communication scenarios in their daily lives. Width investment here formalises and extends this experience — building the conscious, articulable awareness of cultural communication that transforms intuitive competence into transferable expertise.
success_criteria: Participates in a culturally diverse scenario and explains at least two communication decisions
Describes the cultural logic behind each decision

nodes.label: Multimodal bilingual text production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create multimodal bilingual resources — vlogs, educational blogs, subtitled video, interactive guides — that explain cultural meaning and serve a specific audience purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Create a multimodal bilingual resource combining at least two modes, with accurate meaning transfer and appropriate cultural explanation for the intended audience.
nodes.typical_width: Create multimodal bilingual texts — vlogs with subtitles, educational blogs, cultural awareness resources, public signs and notices — paying attention to cultural context; compose bilingual texts for diverse audiences; create resources that explain cultural meaning, not only translate words.
wider: Create a multimodal bilingual resource for a real external audience — evaluate its cultural accuracy and accessibility with a target audience member and revise accordingly

Reflect on the multimodal production process — explain how each mode contributes to meaning, what translation decisions were made, and what the production process revealed about the relationship between the two languages

response_modes.reason: Multimodal bilingual production integrates humour/layered meaning interpretation (node 1) and cultural communication justification (node 2) into a full creative and translation act. The teaching investment is in creating real or realistic audience conditions that require both linguistic accuracy and cultural appropriateness.

success_criteria: Creates a multimodal bilingual resource with accurate meaning transfer in both languages
The resource includes at least one element of cultural explanation — not only translation of words
